subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw board-marked concrete slab-block of 88 loggia apartments on massive tapered pilotis, with rear access galleries, three stair and lift towers, a glazed lobby, and a sculptural rooftop terrace, in the style of Le Corbusier's Unité d'Habitation.
spec.layout:
Static model, no joints. The long slab runs along X (x from -22.8 to 22.8, about 45.6 m wide) and is 14 m deep (z from -7 to 7). The front facade faces +Z. The slab rests on 5 m tall tapered concrete pilotis (y 0..5) and has 8 residential storeys above (y 5..29), then a roof slab (y 29..29.5) with a low parapet (to y 30.2) and the rooftop terrace on top (to y 34 at the mast).

MASTER GRID, which every builder must use. There are 11 bays of 4 m. Bay i (i = 0..10) spans x from -22+4i to -18+4i, so its centre is x = -20+4i. Bay edges, where the cross walls stand, are at x = -22, -18, -14, -10, -6, -2, 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22. Storey k (k = 0..7) has base y = 5+3k. Its floor slab occupies y = 5+3k .. 5+3k+0.35, and the finished floor is 5+3k+0.35. The storey top is 5+3k+3. The front face has loggias: the slab edge is at z = +7 and the recessed loggia back wall is at z = +5 (2 m deep). The rear face has open access galleries: the slab edge is at z = -7 and the rear wall is at z = -5 (2 m deep walkway).

Solid concrete core fill is at x ±21.6, z ±5, y 5..29, so there is no hollow behind the facade planes.

Stair towers: left tower centred at x=+10 and right tower at x=-10, each 5 m wide (x centre ±2.5) and z -11.5..-7, rising from y=0 to 31.4. A central lift tower sits at x -1.5..1.5, z -9.5..-7, y 0..31.0. All three abut the rear gallery edge at z=-7.

STYLE: raw béton brut everywhere. Large chunky masses, deep shadowed recesses, board-marked formwork lines (thin darker horizontal strips on big concrete faces), tie-hole dots, rain-stain streaks running down from slab edges and scuppers, and moss and rust at the base and under drips. Colour is rationed: Corbusier-style polychrome primary panels (red, yellow, blue, green, ochre, white) appear only in the loggia side walls and back panels, the rear doors and the gable mural. Windows glow warm in a scattered handful. Every surface is one flat colour, so build all details as small parts seated 1-3 cm proud of the surface.

PART COUNT RULE FOR ALL BUILDERS: many repeated identical pieces (bays, storeys, doors, ties, streaks) must be merged per colour with mergeGeometries after translating each copy into model space, then added as ONE part per colour with b.part(merged, color, { at: [0,0,0] }). This keeps the part count within each budget. Use SDK extrude, lathe and sweep for the sculptural pieces (pilotis, vaults, stacks, trees). Use rng(seed) for any variation.

parts.builds:
Ground level, y 0..5, under the slab, with the front plaza elements.

(1) Twelve tapered pilotis at x = ±22, ±14, ±6 and z = +4.5 and -4.5. Each is a chunky concrete column about 1.2 m wide at the foot flaring to 1.9 m wide at y=5, 1.4 m deep at the foot and 1.8 m deep at the top. Build them with extrude or frustumBox in the concrete colour. Give each a dark concreteDark plinth foot 0.3 m high, a bulky haunch at the top, 3-4 horizontal boardLine strips on each face, tie-hole dots, rain-stain streaks in concreteStain, and a moss patch at the foot. The end pilotis at x=±22 are wider (to x=±23, a 2 m wide pier) and serve as end buttresses.

(2) A raised glazed lobby box at x -4.5..4.5, z -3..3.5, y 0..4.3 on a 0.45 m high concreteLight plinth. It has a steel-framed glass front wall at z=3.5 with a mullion every 0.9 m, a central double door, a deep concrete surround frame, a lit interior (glassLit panes in places and glassDark in others), a roof edge in concreteLight, a bold mail-box wall in panelYellow and steel, and a black steel sign bar over the door.

(3) A projecting entrance canopy: a flat slab at x -6..6, z 3.5..9, y 4.0..4.4 in concrete with a concreteDark underside strip, held by two stout rectangular piers at x=±5.5, z=8.6. Hanging lamp discs (lamp colour) are set under it.

(4) Four wide concrete steps from z 3.5 to 9.5, each 0.12 m high, in concreteLight with shadow risers, plus concrete cheek walls.

(5) Two glazed shop or community units at x ±(8..13), z -3..3, y 0..3.6. Each has steel mullions, a coloured fascia (panelRed on the left unit, panelBlue on the right), and a canopy slab.

(6) Low concrete planters along the front at z 6.5..8, x ±(8..20), with soil tops and planterGreen shrub blobs. Add a few bollards, 2 lamp posts (steel with lamp heads), and a bike rack in steel.

Stay clear of the slab and rear zone. Tower bases belong to the back part.
parts.attaches: Pilotis tops end at podiumTop (y=5), where the frame's first floor slab begins. The entrance and steps are centred on the entrance mount. Rear pilotis stop at z=-5.4, short of the back part's towers (z < -7).

parts.builds:
The structural concrete skeleton of the residential slab from y=5 to y=30.3.

(1) Eight floor slabs, k=0..7, each x ±22.6, z -7..7, y 5+3k .. 5+3k+0.35, in concrete. Add a thin boardLine strip along each front and rear fascia, and a darker shadow groove line under the slab edges.

(2) The roof slab: x ±22.8, z ±7.1, y 29..29.5, in concreteLight, with a shadow underside strip.

(3) Ten interior cross walls at bay edges x = -18, -14, ..., 18 (thickness 0.4, z from -5 to 7, y from the slab top to the next slab bottom). Merge them. The tops, bottoms and inner faces in the loggias get boardLine strips every 0.3 m.

(4) Two gable end walls, 0.8 m thick (x from 21.8 to 22.6 on the left, mirrored on the right), z -7..7, y 5..29.5. Give them vertical ribs 0.2 m proud at z = every 1.4 m, in concreteDark. They also carry boardLine horizontal courses, a grid of tieHole dots, tall dark slit windows (shadow colour, 0.3 x 3 m) at z=±5.5 on a few storeys, and a big abstract relief mural on each outer face at x=±22.65: z -4..4, y 8..26, made of 5-6 thin plates and one disc in panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue and panelWhite in modulor-like composition.

(5) The solid core fill block: x ±21.6, z ±5, y 5..29, in concreteDark. Merge pieces freely.

(6) The roof parapet: walls 0.4 thick and 0.7 high (y 29.5..30.2) around the perimeter at z=±6.8 and x=±22.4, with a concreteLight cap strip, a moss strip on top, and 6 chunky square scuppers (0.4 x 0.4 x 0.6) projecting from the front and rear parapet faces at x = ±4, ±12, ±20, each with a long rain-stain streak running down the fascia in concreteStain, to about 1.5 m.

(7) Weathering: vertical stain streaks and a few rust drips under scuppers and slab edges, in concreteStain, rust and moss.
parts.attaches: The bottom sits on podiumTop (y=5). The front facade part fills the loggia recesses between frontWall (z=5) and frontFace (z=7). The back part fills the gallery zone from rearWall (z=-5) to rearEdge (z=-7). The roof part stands on roofSlabTop (y=29.5) inside the parapet.

parts.builds:
Everything in the 88 front loggias: bays i=0..10 and storeys k=0..7, in z 5..7.05 on the +Z side. Use the master grid. Let b0 = 5+3k+0.35. Merge repeated pieces per colour.

(a) A balcony parapet panel across each bay front: x edge±0.2, z 6.8..7.0, y b0..b0+1.0, in concrete with a concreteLight cap strip, and 2 boardLine lines. A few parapets (rng seed 11, about 1 in 6) carry a planter box, soil plus planterGreen blobs on top.

(b) Polychrome side walls: on the cross wall faces inside each loggia, thin 0.05 panels at z 5..6.8, y b0..b0+2.7. Each bay gets its left or right side wall painted, and alternate bays use the other side, in a rng-picked colour from panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue, panelGreen, panelWhite and panelOchre. The other side stays bare concrete.

(c) Back wall of each loggia (z=5): a recessed panel 3.3 x 2.6 m (z 5.0..5.06) in concreteLight or a polychrome colour (about 1 in 3 bays, rng).

(d) A window and door set into the back wall: a window 2.0 wide x 1.4 high at x = bay centre - 0.7 with a sill at b0+0.9, in a steel frame 0.06 proud (z up to 5.12) with a glass pane (glass colour; about 1 in 8 panes use glassLit as lit windows, and a few glassDark). A balcony door 0.9 x 2.2 at x = bay centre + 1.2, in a steel frame with glass. Add steel mullions.

(e) Sunscreen details: on storeys 5-7 of every other bay, a deep concrete brise-soleil of 3 horizontal blades (z 6.4..7.0 deep, 0.08 thick, 3.4 wide) under the slab above. Add a vertical concrete fin (0.15 x full height x 0.8 deep) at the centre of every 4th bay.

(f) Fine details: small lamp discs (lamp colour) beside the doors, a few hanging laundry or plant pots as tiny colour boxes, and occasional dark shadow slabs lining the loggia ceilings (shadow colour, 3.6 x 0.02 x 2).

Do NOT rebuild the slabs or cross walls (the frame owns them).
parts.attaches: The back wall sits on the frame core face at frontWall z=5. The parapets sit flush with the slab edge at frontFace z=7. It fits between the frame's slabs (storey base y=5+3k+0.35 up to 5+3k+3) and the cross walls.

parts.builds:
The whole rear side, z from -5 to -11.5, y 0..31.8.

(1) The rear access galleries on all 8 storeys. The walkway is the frame's slab. This part builds the 0.3 thick parapets at z -6.95..-6.65, y b0..b0+1.1, in concrete with a concreteLight cap and a steel rail on top. The parapets run the length x ±22 but leave gaps at the towers (x within 7.5..12.5 and -12.5..-7.5, and x within ±1.5). Build square piers 0.4 x 0.4 at z=-6.8, full storey height, at x = ±22, ±14, ±6, in concrete.

(2) The rear wall cladding at z=-5.0..-5.05 over the core, in concreteLight, plus per bay and storey a door 0.95 x 2.1 at x = bay centre + 1.0 in a rotating colour (panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue, panelGreen, panelOchre, panelWhite, rng seed 23) with a steel frame and a small lamp disc above in the lamp colour. Add a kitchen window 1.0 x 1.0 at x = bay centre - 1.0, sill 1.1 above b0 (glass, with an occasional glassLit), and a mail slot or letter plate. Cross walls are NOT drawn here. The frame owns them.

(3) The two stair towers at towerL and towerR: x centre ±10, width 5, z -11.5..-7, y 0..31.4, in concrete with a boardLine pattern every 0.3 m, tie-hole grids, and stain streaks. Each tower has a tall glazed slot 1.0 wide on the rear face (z=-11.5) running y 1..30, in glassDark, with thin steel diagonal stair stringers and landing lines visible every storey. Add concrete fins on either side. Each storey has a doorway opening, a dark shadow rectangle 1.2 x 2.2 in shadow, on the face toward the gallery at z=-7.02. Each tower has a roof cap slab at y 31.4..31.8 with a 0.3 overhang in concreteLight. A big block numeral built from boxes (1 on the right tower, 2 on the left) in panelRed stands at y 25..28 on the rear face. The ground floor has a steel double door and a canopy slab.

(4) The lift tower at liftTower (x -1.5..1.5, z -9.5..-7, y 0..31.0), narrower and taller, in concreteDark. It has a vertical glass slit window in glassDark and one panelYellow band on its upper stretch, a roof overrun slab, and a ground-floor lift door.

(5) Moss and rust at the tower footings, a few rainwater down pipes (steel) running full height at x = ±16 and ±4 along the rear wall, and stain streaks.
parts.attaches: The gallery parapets and cladding sit on the frame slabs and core face at rearWall (z=-5) and rearEdge (z=-7). The towers butt onto the gallery edge at z=-7. The towers rise from y=0 and the roof part stays above y=29.5 inside z ±6.5, clear of the towers.

parts.builds:
The rooftop terrace on roofSlabTop (y=29.5), inside the parapet (|x| ≤ 21.8, |z| ≤ 6.5). It tops out at y=34.

(1) A gravel deck surface layer, y 29.5..29.6, x ±21.8, z ±6.4, in gravel, with an inner rim edge strip in concreteLight.

(2) A central gym pavilion at x -7..3, z -2.5..4, wall y 29.6..32.3, in concrete with board lines. It has a band of strip windows (glass and steel, a few glassLit) around it, a deep overhanging barrel-vault roof (sweep or extrude a curved profile, apex y 33.2, in concreteLight with a dark underside) and a front door in panelRed.

(3) Two big sculptural ventilation stacks: lathe-built tapered towers with an outward flaring cap, base radius 1.0 narrowing to 0.7 at the neck, 3.5 m high. One is at x=12, z=-3 and one at x=16.5, z=3. Concrete with a concreteDark ring band, a moss collar and a shadow top.

(4) On the left side (x -21..-9), a running track: a flat oval ring of panelOchre with white lane lines. Alongside it sits a shallow paddling pool: a concrete rim ring with a glass-coloured water disc at z=-3, x=-17. Add a sculptural ramp or stair block, a low wall of boards with a slope, at x=-10, z=4.

(5) A water tank: a cylinder (steel and rust) on 4 steel legs at x=-18, z=3.5, 2.2 high. Add a sun-shade pergola with a lattice of thin concreteDark slats on tall posts at x 6..10, z=-4.

(6) A few benches in deckWood on concrete, and 4-5 lollipop trees (trunk in deckWood, round planterGreen canopy) in square concrete planters. Add a tall steel mast with a small flag in panelRed on the pavilion roof at x=-2, z=1, whose top reaches y=34.

(7) Small lamp posts with lamp heads, and a glow-worthy skylight strip (glassLit) on the pavilion roof.
parts.attaches: Rests on roofSlabTop (y=29.5). Everything stays inside the parapet (frame, roofParapetTop y=30.2) and clear of the towers at z < -7.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a spec for a brutalist housing block, a static model with no joints, and I'm working out its real-world scale. I'm weighing a smaller version of something like the Unité d'Habitation, with a width of about 40 m, a height of 30 m, and a length of roughly 16 m, and I'm leaning toward a slab on pilotis with a long facade along x.

I'm laying out the block's parts now: a podium with pilotis and a ground-floor lobby, a main slab of residential floors with recessed loggias on the front, and a grid of eleven 4 m bays set against the floor levels so the different builders line up.

I'm settling the spec into parts: a podium that holds the pilotis and ground-floor lobby, a concrete frame for the slab with floor plates every 3 m, and a facade infill layer that fills the loggia back walls, glazing and balcony parapets on the front.

I'm now setting the four parts' budgets: the podium at 170, the frame at 170, the front facade with its loggia infill at 220, and a rear gallery with the stair and lift towers.

I'm now working out the rooftop pavilion, with a plant room, vent stacks, a water tank, and a small pool, and I'm giving it a budget of 130 and a box that sits just above the main slab.

I'm working out the vertical layout now: the pilotis run from ground to about 5 m, and the floor slabs sit at 3 m intervals above that, each a thin plate at the level where a storey begins. I'm still deciding how the bottom slab rests on the pilotis tops.

I'm fixing the vertical bands: the podium runs from ground to 5 m, and each storey band above it is 3 m tall, with a thin slab at the bottom of each band. The roof sits at 29 m, and I'm still sorting out how the roof slab, the parapet and the rooftop box overlap at the edges.

I'm now placing the bays and cross walls: eleven 4 m bays across the width, with a wall line at each bay edge, the end gables a bit thicker. I'm also working out how the front slab edge sits against the loggia recesses and what depth its fascia should have.

I'm working through how the frame and the facade infill split the depth at the front: the loggia recess sits at about z=5, and I'm checking whether the structural frame needs to fill the full footprint so no gaps show behind the apartments.

I'm treating the frame as a solid central core as well, filling the box between the front infill wall at z=5 and the rear gallery wall at z=-5, in dark concrete from the top of the podium up to the roof. That way the interior doesn't read as hollow from any angle, while the front and back walls are left to the facade and gallery parts.

I'm fixing the core as a solid box inside the footprint so the interior never reads as hollow, with its faces at z=±5 where the infill walls sit. Next I'm placing the front facade's loggia infill: a wall plane at z=5 with door and window frames, and a balcony parapet at z=6.6 to 7.0 across each bay, with the slabs spanning the full depth at 3 m intervals.

I'm working out the loggia infill for each bay: a two-metre window set toward one side, a narrower balcony door beside it, and a coloured panel on the back wall in the polychrome palette.

I'm setting the side panels on the cross-wall faces, each about 0.2 m in from the bay edge and spanning the loggia depth, in the polychrome palette for each bay. Now I'm working on the gallery at the rear, starting with the walkway slab that runs out to z=-7.

I'm now setting the gallery's rear wall: one door per bay at z=-5, plus a small kitchen window, and I'm keeping the cross walls to the span from z=-5 to 7 so the walkway stays open.

I'm deciding where the rear gallery piers go, weighing even spacing every two bays against a layout that keeps the middle symmetric.

I'm placing the stair towers at x=±10 with a 5 m width and a depth running from z=-11.5 to -7, so they reach above the roof, and I'm checking how the gallery bridges connect to them at each storey.

I'm now deciding that the central lift tower sits at x=0, about 3 m wide and running from z=-9.5 to -7, reaching roughly 31 m high. The two stair towers stay as they are, and the gallery parapet is left open where they meet it.

I'm settling on the pilotis layout now, weighing whether to space the columns evenly or keep the arrangement symmetric about the centre.

I'm laying out the pilotis as twelve tapering columns, six along the front and six along the back, each wider at the top and narrowing toward the ground. I'm also placing a glazed lobby box between the columns, with a flat entrance canopy projecting toward the front.

I'm deciding how the ground level meets the street: no plaza slab, just steps and plinth strips, and the end pilotis become massive wall-columns at x=±22 that run down to the ground.

I'm settling where the podium and the back gallery own the stair towers, since their lower sections run down to ground level. I'm also listing the concrete palette colours, from the main grey to the warmer and darker shades.

I'm working through the colour palette now, covering the recess shadow, board lines, tie holes, glass tones and glowing windows, then the steel frames, the painted panel colours, planter greens, soil, weathering moss and rust, roof gravel, and the lamp light.

I'm now assigning the palette its names and checking that it totals 24 colours, dropping one of the warm concretes to get there. I'm also writing the first mount points: the podium's top surface at y=5, the storey bands starting from that level at 3 m intervals, and the front face and wall positions along z.

I'm now setting the mount points for the roof and the tower positions: the roof slab top at y=29.5, the left stair tower at x=+10, and the lift core at the centre, with the entrance at ground level in the middle of the front.

I'm settling the roof: a central rooftop pavilion with a vaulted roof, set between the lift tower and the roof edge, plus two sculptural ventilation stacks.

I'm settling the overall footprint now: the body runs to about x ±24, and I'm weighing whether the end wall piers at each side should be shaped as buttresses that extend that far.

I'm settling the overall footprint: the end walls and slabs reach about 23 m from the centre on each side, so I'm setting the body to a 46 m width and a 34 m height, running from z=-11.5 to 9.5. I'm also checking how the podium's end piers sit at the outer edges and how the floor slabs and gable walls line up with them.

I'm now going through the frame's finishing details: exposed vertical ribs and relief panels on the end gables, board lines and tie-hole dots on the walls, darker streaks under the slab edges, moss along the parapet, and chunky square scuppers. I'm giving the frame a budget of 170 and keeping its joints static.

I'm now assigning the part boxes: the podium runs across the front from z=-6 to 9.5 with its pilotis, and the back gallery with the tower bases takes the rear section down to z=-11.5.

Next I'm checking the box bounds for the back part, which runs from z=-11.5 to -5 and rises to about 31.8 m, so it doesn't overlap the podium's lower band. Then I'm setting the frame box to span x ±23 and z -7 to 7, and the front facade to sit just in front of it, from z=5 to 7.05.

I'm writing out the facade details now: window and door frames per bay on each storey, with a coloured spandrel panel below the glazing.

I'm specifying the loggia infill for each bay: a full-height coloured panel on the back wall, with a window and a balcony door set into it. The balcony parapet on the front will be a concrete band with the coloured side walls alternating by bay.

I'm working out how to fit the facade within its 220 budget: a dozen small parts per bay and storey would blow past it, so I'm planning to merge the glazing, panels and parapets into a few geometries grouped by colour.

I'm merging the repeated facade pieces into one part per colour, so the roughly 88 bay-storey elements stay within the 900-part limit. I'm also adding some variation with lit windows that glow, and planning the rear gallery's doors, windows, parapets, piers, stair towers, and lift tower.

I'm now laying out the podium's details: twelve tapered pilotis, six along the front and six along the back, set at x=±22, ±14 and ±6 and at z=±4.5. The front row sits inside the front depth, and I'm finishing the ribs, plinths and capitals with their concrete colours.

I'm placing the lobby between the front pilotis, a glazed box with steel mullions, a central double door and a canopy, and I'm also planning two shop units on either side that stay clear of the columns at x=±14.

I'm adding steps up to the lobby, a raised plinth, planters and lamp posts along the front, and a bike rack. I'm also giving the pilotis a moss and stain wash at the base, and setting the part budgets to total 890.

I'm setting the mount points for the front and rear walls, the podium top, the roof slab, and the two stair towers and lift core, with the entrance at ground level and a roof parapet rising to about 30.2 m.

I'm placing the rear wall's cladding panels in lighter concrete at z=-5, and I'm checking that the stair and lift towers close off the back correctly. The frame core's ends sit at x=±21.6, and I'm turning to the facade's colour assignment, starting with the bay palette in red, yellow, blue and green.

I'm planning the frame's slabs now: eight floor plates in concrete, each 0.35 m thick, stacked at 3 m intervals starting from the podium top at y=5, plus a roof slab at 29 to 29.5 with a dark drip edge underneath.

I'm laying out the cross walls, twelve of them spaced every 4 m across the width, running from z=-5 to 7 between the slabs. The two end gables get thicker walls with vertical relief ribs and a stepped mural in red, yellow and blue on their outer faces.

I'm now adding the gable details: a few stepped relief shapes on the outer faces, narrow dark window slits, and a grid of tie-hole dots. Then I'm finishing the roof parapet with chunky square scuppers and some stain streaks, plus board lines on the fascia.

I'm laying out the roof now: a gravel surface over the deck, a gym pavilion with a curved roof set near the centre, and two large ventilation stacks.

I'm now sketching the roof's layout: the ventilation stacks, a water tank on legs, and a running track or paddling pool on either side, with the gym pavilion in the middle.

I'm adding the last of the roof details: a gravel-topped deck with a gym pavilion, a lattice pergola, a flagpole, a play sculpture, benches, and lollipop trees in planters, at a budget of 140. I'm also setting the rear gallery's parapet as a thin concrete band at z -7 to -6.65, rising a metre above the gallery floor and leaving a gap where the stair towers sit.

I'm placing the stair tower details now, with a tall glazed slot on each tower face so the stair flights show through as diagonal lines. Next are the gallery doors per bay and their small windows, sills and lamps.

I'm now sketching the stair tower faces with tall glazed slots and diagonal steel stair lines, adding a cap slab with overhang, a door at ground, and bold block numerals on each tower. Then I'll write the spec as JSON with no joints.
